title: Decide whether Chatticus keeps Cognito as the Google sign-in broker
description:
Raised by Ryan 2026-10-01, mid-deploy of the development environment (fd3724): 'I never wanted a Cognito User pool. We're using Google for authentication.'

## Fact
The existing design (card 0df6cb, closed; infra/lib/auth-stack.ts) puts a Cognito user pool BETWEEN the app and Google: Google is the only identity provider but Cognito is the OIDC broker the web app talks to (authorization code + PKCE, a public app client with no secret, custom domain auth-dev/-staging/auth). The API verifies Cognito-issued ID tokens (CognitoJwtVerifier, resolve_me_from_token); identity is keyed on verified email, never the Cognito sub. The Google redirect URI /oauth2/idpresponse belongs to Cognito. Legacy development, staging and production all work this way, and the design predates the migration. It was carried into the new dedicated-account stack unchanged; Ryan was not asked.

## State at the moment of the objection
ChatticusAuth was just deployed into chatticus-development: one user pool with ZERO users, one app client, the Google identity provider, the custom domain auth-develop.chattic.us, two alias records, three SSM parameters. Web is NOT deployed (it reads the Cognito ids from SSM). Nothing depends on it yet. Cognito costs nothing at idle and has a free tier far above this use.

## Options
A. Keep Cognito (status quo): no code change; consistent with legacy; the new dev environment finishes as designed.
B. Remove Cognito and have the app use Google directly. Work: web OIDC settings (buildUserManagerSettings authority, silent renew, sign-out), the API's token verifier (verify Google ID tokens: issuer, audience, JWKS), drop AuthStack plus its zone, certificate, SSM parameters and DNS, new redirect URIs. CAUTION (to be verified before committing): as far as I know Google's web-application OAuth clients require a client secret at the token step, which a browser app cannot hold, and that is the usual reason a broker like Cognito sits in the middle; the browser-only alternative is Google Identity Services, which returns short-lived ID tokens without refresh. That would change the session and sign-out behaviour users see.
C. Keep Cognito for now, schedule B as its own piece of work after the environment moves.

## Needs
Ryan's choice. Until then: do not deploy the dev web stack; do not change legacy. If B is chosen the just-deployed dev auth stack is torn down through CDK (no users, no data to lose).

comments.author: home
comments.text: Ryan (2026-10-01): 'We need to use Cognito. We do not want a Cognito User pool. We do not want to be responsible for managing Cognito users.' Interpreted as: Cognito as the broker, but no Cognito-managed users. Evidence from the code and the deployed dev pool (chatticus-development): selfSignUpEnabled false, signInAliases email only, no MFA, app client supports ONLY the Google identity provider with the authorization-code flow and no secret, no native password flows (ExplicitAuthFlows null), 0 users. So nobody can create, sign in as, or administer a Cognito-native user; the only way a record exists is a Google sign-in creating a federated shadow record (email, sub, no password, no lifecycle). Membership and roles live in DynamoDB, not Cognito. A user pool is the container Cognito requires to broker an external provider and issue the OIDC tokens the app and API consume; Cognito identity pools give AWS credentials, not these tokens, so there is no 'Cognito without a user pool' for this flow. Remaining responsibility is small: shadow records accumulate one per person who has signed in (a person's deletion request would mean deleting their shadow record). The only way to have no Cognito resource at all is option B (Google directly), a real change with the client-secret caveat. AWAITING Ryan's confirmation that the broker-only pool is acceptable; if so the dev environment continues with web.

right_now_summary: Ryan must confirm that Cognito may broker Google sign-in without managing native users.
